title: Getting Started with React Hooks
transcript:
[00:00] Hey everyone, welcome back to the channel, today we are talking about React Hooks
[00:10] Before Hooks, sharing stateful logic between components required render props or higher-order components
[00:24] Hooks let you use state and lifecycle features without writing a class
[00:36] The first hook you should know is useState, it returns a pair of the current value and a setter function
[00:50] You can call the setter with a new value directly, or with a function that receives the previous value
[01:04] The second hook is useEffect, it runs after the component renders
[01:14] If you pass an empty dependency array, the effect only runs once after the first render
[01:28] If you return a function from useEffect, React calls it during cleanup, which is great for removing event listeners
[01:42] The third hook is useRef, the value is stored in a ref object and changing it does not trigger a re-render
[01:56] useRef is often used to access DOM elements directly
[02:08] Custom hooks are just functions that start with the word use, they can call other hooks inside
[02:22] The most important rule is that hooks must be called at the top level, never inside loops or conditions
[02:38] If you break this rule, React will throw an error about the order of hooks
[02:50] There is also a lint plugin called eslint-plugin-react-hooks that catches most violations automatically
[03:05] That is the overview, in the next video we will build a real project with these hooks
[03:14] Thanks for watching, and see you in the next one
referencePoints: Hooks 之前共享有状态逻辑需要 render props 或高阶组件
Hooks 允许不写 class 就使用 state 和生命周期特性
useState 返回当前值和 setter 函数
useEffect 在组件渲染之后运行
空依赖数组让 effect 只在首次渲染后运行一次
useEffect 返回的函数会在 cleanup 时调用
useRef 的值改变不会触发重新渲染
自定义 hook 是以 use 开头的函数
hooks 必须写在顶层，不能放在循环或条件里
eslint-plugin-react-hooks 能自动发现大部分违规
